title: Print a shipping label from an order webhook
examObjective: Applying correct syntax to write DataWeave transformations to coerce, format, order, and filter data
basics: A selector such as `payload.customer.name` walks into nested data one key at a time. Writing `{ key: value, ... }` builds a new object with exactly the fields you list, in the order you list them. Most DataWeave you will write is these two things together: pick values out, put them into a new shape.
prompt:
An order webhook arrives from the web shop. The label printer needs a flat object with exactly four fields: `orderId`, `name`, `city` and `postcode`.

Some orders are sent before the customer has entered an address, and some before the customer is known at all. The label must still have all four fields. Anything the order does not have yet is `null`. Never an empty string.
hints: Four fields, four selectors. Write the object you want and fill each value in with a path into the payload.
Try the selector on the second hidden shape in your head: what does selecting `city` from a null address give you?
Selecting from null gives null, not an error, so no guard is needed. Adding `default ""` is what breaks it.
solution:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
{
  orderId: payload.id,
  name: payload.customer.name,
  city: payload.customer.address.city,
  postcode: payload.customer.address.postcode
}

mustFail.why: falls back to an empty string, so a missing address prints as blank fields instead of null
mustFail.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
{
  orderId: payload.id,
  name: payload.customer.name default "",
  city: payload.customer.address.city default "",
  postcode: payload.customer.address.postcode default ""
}

mustFail.why: guards against a missing address by leaving the fields out, so the label is missing keys instead of having nulls
mustFail.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
{
  orderId: payload.id,
  name: payload.customer.name,
  (city: payload.customer.address.city) if (payload.customer.address != null),
  (postcode: payload.customer.address.postcode) if (payload.customer.address != null)
}

explanation.approach: Selectors are null-safe: selecting a field from null, or from a field that is not there, gives null all the way down. So the straightforward object already handles the missing address and the missing customer. The two ways to get this wrong are both extra code: a `default` that turns null into "", and a condition that drops the key.

snippets.label: Selecting through a null address
snippets.note: No error. The key is written, with a null value.

snippets.label: Selecting through a missing customer
snippets.note: Three levels into nothing is still just null.

snippets.label: What default "" does to it
snippets.note: An empty String is a value. The printer cannot tell "not known yet" from "blank".
